qti-assessment-test.title: Clearly Clinical - IFS Therapist Reactivity in Suicide Risk & Neurodiversity-Affirming Care CE (Demo)

qti-assessment-item.title: Differentiate clinician manager-part countertransference reactivity from Self-led collaborative suicide risk formulation during acute ideation.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_1): Differentiate clinician manager-part countertransference reactivity from Self-led collaborative suicide risk formulation during acute ideation.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: A client states, 'Part of me keeps thinking everyone would be relieved if I went to sleep and never woke up.' Which therapist response integrates Self-led IFS regulation with ethical suicide-risk assessment?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Acknowledge how exhausted that part feels without panic, then conduct a transparent C-SSRS inquiry into active intent, plan, and access to lethal means
Immediately terminate therapeutic dialogue and call emergency transport before asking whether the client has suicidal intent or a plan
Explore childhood attachment metaphors exclusively and omit direct lethality questions to avoid triggering clinician anxiety
Require the client to sign a standalone 'no-suicide contract' in lieu of a collaborative safety plan

qti-content-body.p: Verified: Grounded curiosity keeps disclosure open while fulfilling the non-negotiable clinical duty to assess intent, plan, and lethal means.
Diagnostic rationale: Automatic involuntary transport for passive ideation without lethality assessment escalates trauma and erodes therapeutic trust.
Diagnostic rationale: Omitting structured lethality triage when suicidal ideation is disclosed breaches behavioral health standard of care.
Diagnostic rationale: Empirical literature demonstrates standalone 'no-suicide contracts' lack protective efficacy and never replace Stanley-Brown safety planning.

qti-assessment-item.title: Document structured C-SSRS lethality triage, lethal-means counseling, and Stanley-Brown safety planning alongside pharmacotherapy coordination.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_2): Document structured C-SSRS lethality triage, lethal-means counseling, and Stanley-Brown safety planning alongside pharmacotherapy coordination.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: When documenting an outpatient high-stakes session involving passive suicidal ideation without imminent intent, plus a recent primary-care dose change of sertraline (Zoloft), which progress-note elements satisfy utilization and risk-management standards?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Objective C-SSRS risk/protective factors, completed Stanley-Brown safety plan steps, lethal-means counseling, crisis line resources (988), and ROI-consented prescriber coordination
A brief one-line entry stating 'Client safe at departure; will reassess next Tuesday'
Verbatim process notes of unrelated family dreams with zero mention of lethal-means inquiry
Instructing the client to abruptly discontinue sertraline (Zoloft) without contacting the prescribing physician

qti-content-body.p: Verified: Comprehensive risk-protective formulation, concrete safety plan documentation, lethal-means restriction, and prescriber coordination establish defensible care.
Diagnostic rationale: Conclusory 'client safe' notes without objective C-SSRS findings or safety-plan steps fail clinical and legal documentation standards.
Diagnostic rationale: Omitting lethal-means assessment and protective factor documentation leaves critical clinical risk unaddressed.
Diagnostic rationale: Non-prescribing psychotherapists must never direct medication discontinuation; they coordinate via authorized prescriber communication.

qti-assessment-item.title: Modify Internal Family Systems language and sensory-predictability scaffolds for autistic clients experiencing alexithymia or masking fatigue.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_3): Modify Internal Family Systems language and sensory-predictability scaffolds for autistic clients experiencing alexithymia or masking fatigue.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: An autistic client freezes when asked, 'Go inside and tell me what sensation shows up in your chest.' Which neurodiversity-affirming IFS adaptation best reduces uncertainty?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Interpret the freeze as treatment resistance from a defiant protector part and repeat the somatic prompt louder
Offer concrete externalized options such as visual cards, written descriptors, or cognitive thoughts/action urges instead of requiring interoceptive metaphors
Attempt to 'unburden' the client's lifelong autistic sensory sensitivities and hand-flapping stims as trauma exiles
Abandon collaborative goal-setting and switch to unannounced exposure exercises without consent

qti-content-body.p: Diagnostic rationale: Mislabeling alexithymia or processing latency as defiance compounds clinical shame and misattunement.
Verified: Externalized visual or cognitive-behavioral anchors accommodate interoceptive differences and reduce ambiguous-prompt overwhelm.
Diagnostic rationale: Neurodevelopmental traits and regulatory stims are core neurology to affirm, never pathology or 'parts' to eliminate.
Diagnostic rationale: Unpredictable, non-consensual interventions heighten autonomic threat and violate affirming practice.

qti-assessment-item.title: Modify Internal Family Systems language and sensory-predictability scaffolds for autistic clients experiencing alexithymia or masking fatigue.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_3): Modify Internal Family Systems language and sensory-predictability scaffolds for autistic clients experiencing alexithymia or masking fatigue.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: In neurodiversity-affirming IFS therapy, how should a clinician conceptualize an autistic adult's chronic social masking part versus sensory meltdowns?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Treat chronic masking as an adaptive manager role developed to navigate social rejection, while addressing sensory meltdowns through environmental load reduction rather than parts unburdening
Demand immediate 100 percent unmasking across unsafe workplaces without assessing real-world safety consequences
Classify sensory meltdowns as manipulative behavior warranting extinction contingencies
Frame autism itself as a dissociative subpersonality caused by early parenting

qti-content-body.p: Verified: Masking functions as an understandable protective adaptation with high energy cost, whereas sensory meltdowns reflect neurological overload requiring sensory accommodations.
Diagnostic rationale: Forced unmasking in unsupportive environments ignores real discrimination risks and violates IFS respect for protective pacing.
Diagnostic rationale: Sensory meltdowns are involuntary autonomic/sensory overwhelm responses, never operant manipulation.
Diagnostic rationale: Framing autism as psychogenic or parenting-induced is scientifically discredited and harmful.
